strengths: Identifies the correct excitatory/glutamatergic identity with direct marker support from GRIA2, NEUROD2, NEUROD6, FEZF2 and SOX5.
Correctly uses pan-neuronal markers (SYT1, SNAP25, STMN2, TUBB2A, EEF1A2) and does not over-interpret NR4A2/SNCA as dopaminergic.
weaknesses: Includes weakly supported dopaminergic/retinal lineage speculations despite absence of TH, SLC6A3 and retinal core markers.
Partially relies on tissue-context reasoning not present in the original evidence.

strengths: Conservative and well-supported by pan-neuronal markers SYT1, SNAP25, STMN2, TUBB2A and EEF1A2.
weaknesses: Under-specified: does not refine to the glutamatergic neuron descendant despite rank-2 candidate and direct support from GRIA2, NEUROD2 and NEUROD6.
Ignores excitatory-specific markers in its top1 label.

strengths: Directly uses glutamatergic markers GRIA2, NEUROD2 and NEUROD6, plus deep-layer markers FEZF2 and SOX5.
Correctly excludes glial, interneuron and progenitor alternatives based on absent markers.
weaknesses: Some supporting terms are pan-neuronal rather than strictly glutamatergic-specific.
Less detailed subtype reasoning than cassia, but reaches the same valid CLID.

supporting: GRIA2 encodes an AMPA glutamate receptor subunit and directly supports glutamatergic/excitatory neuron identity.
NEUROD2 and NEUROD6 are proneural transcription factors supporting glutamatergic neuron differentiation.
FEZF2 and SOX5 support deep-layer cortical excitatory/projection neuron features consistent with glutamatergic identity.
Pan-neuronal markers SYT1, SNAP25, STMN2, TUBB2A and EEF1A2 support neuron identity.
conflicting: NR4A2 and SNCA are dopaminergic-associated markers but lack TH and SLC6A3, so they do not override the dominant glutamatergic signature.
Weak epithelial program marker CDH7 is not supported by the overall cluster profile and does not indicate a separate lineage.
enrichment_or_literature: Original enrichment observations such as Glutamate Neurotransmitter Release Cycle, Transmission across Chemical Synapses, forebrain development and neuron migration are consistent with a glutamatergic neuron identity; no external PMIDs are required.

provenance.note: Publication-facing final decision, QC disposition and evaluation fields are synchronized to the submitted Supplementary Data.
